Round 2 · Implementation · Medium

Ticket #03 — Password Reset Flow

Difficulty: Medium

Context

You maintain account recovery for a member portal. A reset token is the ID in a password-reset link. Each token has an expiration time and may change a password once. The service receives a clock, so tests can choose the time directly.

Practice report

At 12:00 on 2030-01-01, issue token first for u1, then issue second for the same user before either token is used. Call reset("first", "old-path").

Observation Current starter Expected
Reset result True False
Stored password hash for u1, initially absent "old-path" Still absent

The newer token should remain usable after the rejected attempt with first.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Issued tokens have a fixed lifetime (20 minutes by default). A token is valid before its expiration and invalid at the exact expiration instant and afterward.
  • Issuing a newer token invalidates earlier unused tokens for that user without affecting tokens belonging to other users.
  • A successful reset changes the stored password hash and consumes the token once. A repeated use cannot replace that password again.
  • Unknown, expired, used, or invalidated tokens and an empty replacement hash leave the stored password unchanged. Invalid issuance or an existing token ID must not replace a token.
  • Test time boundaries by controlling the supplied clock, without real waits.

Out of Scope

Work with the supplied token IDs and password-hash strings. Email delivery, password hashing, token generation, and a production authentication system are outside this exercise.

Investigation

Trace issuance and reset through the token repository and service. Prove the old-link case, the usable newer link, single use, and the expiration boundary by asserting both results and stored passwords. Keep the correction focused on this lifecycle.
